stem: A child is behind on the recommended vaccination schedule. Which principle should guide catch-up vaccination?

options.A: Permanently skip delayed vaccine doses because they cannot be given later.
options.B: Use the CDC catch-up schedule; a vaccine series generally does not need to be restarted because of an extended interval between doses.
options.C: Restart every vaccine series from dose 1 whenever the recommended interval has been exceeded.
options.D: Avoid catch-up vaccination because delayed schedules are not recommended for children.

rationale: CDC's current child and adolescent catch-up schedule states that a vaccine series does not need to be restarted regardless of the time elapsed between doses. The age-appropriate catch-up table and accompanying schedule notes should be used to determine which doses and minimum intervals are needed. Therefore B is correct.
educational_objective: Apply the CDC catch-up immunization principle that extended intervals do not require restarting a properly begun vaccine series.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Catch-up Immunization Schedule for Children and Adolescents
source_version_date: Current CDC page; Addendum updated July 2, 2025; currentness rechecked August 17, 2026
source_locator: Vaccine Catch-Up Guidance; Children age 4 months through 6 years — introductory statement before Table 2
source_claim_supported: For children whose vaccinations have been delayed, vaccine series do not need to be restarted regardless of elapsed time between doses; use the age-appropriate CDC catch-up schedule and notes.
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — immunization and age-appropriate preventive care
correction_summary: Rechecked the temporally unstable CDC immunization schedule on August 17, 2026. The current CDC catch-up page still carries the July 2, 2025 addendum and explicitly retains the no-restart rule. Tightened the wording to avoid implying that every delayed vaccine is always given without age-specific exceptions. Easy difficulty retained.
audit_findings: Current CDC catch-up page directly supports B. The wording 'generally' and reference to age-appropriate tables/notes avoid overgeneralizing vaccine-specific age limits. A, C and D contradict CDC guidance. Independent second pass passed.
